newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel offers houses in Jewish settlements.
newsitem.headline: Israel offers houses in Jewish settlements.

text.p: The Israeli government published a newspaper advertisement on Tuesday offering houses for sale in 30 Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

"You can build on this ad," said the Housing Ministry advertisement in the mass circulation Maariv daily, offering an unspecified number of private homes across the West Bank and in the Katif settlement zone in the Gaza Strip.

The advertisement, reminiscent of sales campaigns launched in the 1980s by previous right-wing Likud governments, listed the names and telephone numbers of 30 settlements in which it said private homes were available.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who took office in June, has pledged to expand existing Jewish settlements on land Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war but has stopped short of approving any new outposts.
The PLO has called the policy a violation of its peace deals with Israel. The United States has described the settlements as obstacles to peace.

The Haaretz newspaper reported on Tuesday that the Housing Ministry intended to market land in the West Bank and Gaza Strip for the private-sector construction this year of 4,553 housing units for Israelis.
The report said final approval for the land programme, in which existing settlements would be widened, rested with Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
A Housing Ministry spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
More than 130,000 Jews have settled among some two million Arabs in the West Bank and Gaza since 1967.
